html:
SMTO-AUT-0036 — Too many Google sign-ins are waiting to be finished

GUID: ecaab131-b31a-5394-994e-554030cfada1
Slug: google-oauth-too-many-pending
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • SMTO can keep up to 32 unfinished Google sign-in links at once, and that limit is reached, so no new link was made. Unfinished links expire after ten minutes. None of your Google accounts were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you already have a Google sign-in page open from SMTO, finish it in that browser tab. Each finished sign-in frees a place for a new one.
  2. Otherwise, wait ten minutes before asking SMTO to connect Google again. Unfinished sign-in links expire after ten minutes and are then removed from the waiting list.
  3. If you didn't start these sign-ins, look for a running Task that keeps asking to connect Google and select Stop. If a Schedule does this, pause it on the Schedules page. A Task or Schedule that requests a connection over and over can fill every place on its own.
  4. Then ask SMTO to connect Google once, and finish that sign-in before starting another one. Handling one sign-in at a time keeps you under the limit and avoids linking the wrong account.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a new Google sign-in link, and finishing it shows the account as connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; sign-ins started by other people using the same SMTO count toward this limit too. Don't keep requesting new links, because each request adds to the queue.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • BrowserOAuth.start refused a new Google consent handshake because the provider already holds its maximum of 32 unexpired pending handshakes, each valid for ten minutes.

What this means

  • The shared browser authorization owner already holds its maximum 32 unexpired pending handshakes. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The shared browser authorization owner already holds its maximum 32 unexpired pending handshakes.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current pending authorization requests and their ten-minute expiries.

How to fix it

  • Complete existing handshakes or let them expire (600 seconds each; they live only in Server process memory and are also discarded on Server restart, which invalidates every outstanding link). Look for a Task or Schedule looping on auth.google_connect or google_calendar.connect, stop it, then start a single new consent.
  • Complete a pending authorization or wait for its ten-minute expiry before starting another.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • Pending handshakes fall below the bound and a new intended request receives its own state.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
